I'm H., HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. Sarah passed the hardware side over to me.

Good troubleshooting on your end, that USB test rules the screen out, so the display is fine and something upstream is not driving it. Fans spinning tells me the board is getting power, and no heat tells me the chips never started.

Two things decide this, and the first one matters most:

1. Do you remember what the error on the screen actually said? Even a few words ("VREG", "overheat", "0 chips", a number) points straight at the cause.
2. With the miner plugged in and the fans running, is it still showing up on your network? Check your router's client list or your mining pool for the worker coming online. If it gets an IP, open its web UI in a browser and tell me what the ASIC / chip count reads.

If it still answers on the network, the board is alive and this is likely fixable. Start with whichever of those two you can get me first.

Searched the web · NerdQAxe NerdOctaxe Guru Meditation Error 0xffffffff screen
Searched the web · ESP32 "Guru Meditation Error" 0xffffffff LoadProhibited mean

Thanks, that code helps more than you'd think.

What I found, so you know where it comes from: on the NerdQAxe firmware (shufps/ESP-Miner-NerdQAxePlus, the code your Octaxe runs) that message is printed by the miner itself, and it appears as 
"PSU error - Guru Meditation #····" on a NerdQaxe++ in issue 271 of that project
. So the number after "Guru Meditation" is a status word the firmware read back from the power stage, and an all-F value (0xFFFFFFFF) is what you get when that read comes back with nothing on the bus, meaning the power side did not answer.

That fits exactly what you see: the controller panics at boot before it can init the display (so the screen stays dark even though the screen is good) and the chips never get voltage (so no heat), while the fans run because they are fed directly.

Two causes look the same here: an underpowered or failing power brick, or the on-board regulator. We rule out the cheap one first.

Next step, one thing: what power supply are you running it on, and do you have another one you can try? For the Octaxe you want a solid barrel supply at the rated voltage and at least the rated amps, not a phone charger or a weak brick. Tell me what is printed on your brick (volts and amps) and whether you have a spare to swap in.
